tasks.name: Misleading name: checkAppointment
tasks.description: The function checkAppointment sounds like it only performs a check. Does it change anything? If so, what, and where?
tasks.answerKey: It changes state. After checking eligibility, slot existence, availability and service coverage, it creates an appointment and mutates the chosen slot in place by assigning slot.bookedReferralId (validation.ts:36). It also emits appointment:booked (37-40) before returning. 1 point for identifying the mutation with the file named; naming the event is not required. Marker note: a second emission, eligibility:failed, sits on the failure path at 14-18, so a participant may name a different event without affecting the score. Foil: reserveSlot at scheduling/service.ts:21-25 returns a copy and mutates nothing.

tasks.name: Cross-cutting concern: eligibility
tasks.description: Eligibility is checked in more than one place in this codebase. Find every place in the application where it happens. Test files do not count.
tasks.answerKey: checkEligibility is called from exactly three production sites: accepting a referral (useClinicStore.ts:52), booking an appointment (validation.ts:12), and reverification (nightlyReverification.ts:19). Definition at triage/eligibility.ts:4-25. Verified complete: checkEligibility has exactly three importers, and the five unindexed files (.gitignore, .gitkeep, LICENSE, tsconfig.node.json, vite.config.ts) cannot contain a fourth. 1 point only for all three; two of three is incorrect. Marker note: bookAppointment in the store (108-142) reaches eligibility transitively through checkAppointment, so naming the store action for that site scores the point.

tasks.name: Applied: add a new referral type
tasks.description: A new referral type is to be added. Where would you add it, and what else would have to change for the application to work? Write your answer down.
tasks.answerKey: Required to compile, four changes: (1) add the literal to ReferralType, domain.ts:1; (2) add a complete entry to referralPolicies, a Record<ReferralType, ReferralPolicy>, priorityRules.ts:26-31; (3) extend the object literal inside humaniseType, format.ts:17-24 (literal 18-23); (4) add a route module registering a handler, since routeReferral throws at runtime for an unregistered type. The loader discovers it automatically. Required to be usable but not to compile, recorded and not scored: registry.test.ts:7-8 asserts toBe(4) and will fail; the pathway filter is hardcoded at ReferralListPage.tsx:83-88; the type badge (ReferralDetailPage.tsx:120) and dot (ReferralTable.tsx:45) fall back to base CSS. Needs no change: useReferralFilters.ts widens automatically. Scoring 0-2: 1 for the correct insertion point (ReferralType); 1 for at least two further changes from the required-to-compile list, with written justification.

tasks.name: Retention: where a slot is booked
tasks.description: Without looking, where in this codebase does a slot actually get booked, and what makes that surprising?
tasks.answerKey: Inside checkAppointment (validation.ts:36), which mutates slot.bookedReferralId. Surprising because the assignment happens inside a function named as a check. Scoring 0-2, marked independently of task 1: 1 for the correct location; 1 for articulating why it is surprising, with written justification.
